The Loop

Agentic AI · React, FastAPI, SQLite, Groq

The Loop builds websites through four stages: plan, generate, evaluate, and improve. Each pass leaves a draft and an evaluation record so you can see what changed and keep the best version.

How evaluation and recovery work
  • Deterministic checks and a model rubric score each draft. The evaluation criteria are frozen when the run starts.
  • The persistent queue restores pending jobs after a restart. Interrupted runs keep their drafts without automatically replaying paid inference.
  • Generated HTML opens in a sandbox. Per-user ownership checks protect saved projects, and evaluation profiles support rollback.

The worker runs as a single instance and checks for cancellation between stages.

StorySeed

Generative AI · Tokenization, causal attention, evaluation

I trained a small English story model from random initialization. The work moved from a character baseline through byte-pair encoding, causal attention, a decoder, and repeatable evaluation.

Training and evaluation results
8.47M
Model parameters
4,096
BPE vocabulary
256
Token context

The recovery model trained for 48,000 updates. On the same 200 reserved stories, bits per UTF-8 byte decreased from 1.708 to 0.626. The comparison measures the combined changes. Story coherence remains experimental, and the trained weights stay local.

Relay

Real-time messaging · Next.js, FastAPI, SQLite

Relay uses authenticated WebSockets and persistent conversations. Client-generated message IDs let a user retry sending a message without creating a duplicate.

Persistence, delivery, and deployment

The backend uses SQLAlchemy, SQLite in WAL mode, and Alembic migrations. Session tokens are hashed, and group administration has explicit authorization checks.

The Azure deployment used Docker Compose, Caddy TLS, health checks, and backups. The educational Signal-inspired build uses mocked verification and server-side message storage.

Local data and recovery

How I work

Three decisions that recur across my projects.

Design for retries and interruptions

In Relay, the same message ID can safely be sent again. In The Loop, a restart restores queued work and retains incomplete drafts so a paid inference call isn’t silently repeated.

Relay deliveryThe Loop recovery

Make comparisons repeatable

StorySeed’s recovery evaluation compares both models on the same reserved stories. The Loop freezes a run’s criteria so later edits to a profile leave the original comparison intact.

StorySeed evaluation

Leave evidence people can inspect

At Munshot, I built dashboards for extraction accuracy and failure patterns. The Loop saves drafts, scores, and version history so a reviewer can trace the result through each stage.
